note: The human half of §12.4's overlay: why a source path the plan never named is nevertheless inside its epic's scope. Keyed `<epic> <path>`. Entries marked HOT ZONE touch a file §2.D lists as shared, and the delegate reads those individually rather than accepting the sentence.

reasons.P0-03 scripts/architecture/capability-se: The seam-classification rules themselves. The registry declared the checker but not the module holding the rules it applies, and a frozen case naming a classification has to name where that classification is decided.
reasons.P0-03 scripts/architecture/check-capabil: The declaration file for the .mjs checker. Repo convention pairs every scripts/*.mjs with a .d.mts so TypeScript consumers see its API; the registry named only the runtime half.
reasons.P0-04 scripts/architecture/layer-order.t: The canonical layer sequence and edge-classification rules must[0] is about. The registry declared the scanner (a later stage) and not the contract module the scanner applies.
reasons.P0-08 benchmarks/harness-capability/scen: The scenario table the fault-matrix cases enumerate. A benchmark scenario list is neither test nor product source, and the registry file list has no benchmarks/ entry at all.
reasons.P1-01 packages/plugin/plugin-manifest/sr: The published ./invariant companion. Package rules require the companion to live beside the manifest module it observes; the registry declared the manifest module alone.
reasons.P1-02 packages/host/plugin-inventory/src: The consumer that reads recorded provenance in production. must[2] is about verification reaching a real inventory, and the inventory is where that call site lives.
reasons.P1-02 packages/kernel/trust-kernel/src/i: The signature roots provenance verification is checked against. HOT ZONE: the kernel entry point is shared with P0-02 and P2-02, and this epic reads from it rather than changing its construction.
reasons.P1-03 packages/plugin/plugin-lock/src/ca: Candidate-lock construction, which is half of must[0]: a lock that pins integrity has to be built somewhere, and the registry declared only the comparison side.
reasons.P1-03 packages/plugin/plugin-lock/src/co: The atomic commit path. must[0] requires the lock to be written durably; the registry named the decision functions and not the write.
reasons.P1-03 packages/plugin/plugin-lock/src/ga: The boot-admission decision the U stage proves. The registry declared the lock package broadly and this file is where admission is decided.
reasons.P1-03 packages/plugin/plugin-lock/src/lo: Created by this epic to close BLOCKED-135: real integrity read from pnpm-lock.yaml, replacing a `dsh.provenance.integrity` field nothing wrote. The plan predates the finding, so it could not have named the file.
reasons.P1-03 scripts/first100/verify-boot-path-: The structural gate §12.1 substituted for the withdrawn fetch-spy assertion: the boot closure contains no HTTP client. It is program infrastructure the epic was told to build, not product code.
reasons.P1-07 packages/skill/skill-filesystem/sr: The provider whose filesystem access the trust decision gates. The clause is about what a skill may reach, and this is the reaching.
reasons.P1-07 packages/workspace/workspace-trust: The local trust store the decision reads. The registry declared the policy and not the store it consults.
reasons.P1-08 apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts: HOT ZONE: the boot path where a compatibility refusal actually stops a launch. The clause is about boot admission, so the assertion has to reach the real boot rather than the solver alone.
reasons.P1-09 packages/extensions/cordis-host-ru: The runtime guard that attributes a tool call to its owning plugin. Ownership is decided here, and the registry named only the attribution rules.
The host runner entry that installs the guard above. Its registration is what puts attribution on the live path.
reasons.P1-09 packages/extensions/tool-cordis/sr: The catalog surface whose entries carry owner attribution to the model.
reasons.P1-09 scripts/gen-cordis-catalog.ts: The generator that produces the catalog the case reads. A generated artifact cannot be frozen without naming its generator.
reasons.P2-01 packages/identity/principal/src/in: The published ./invariant companion for the principal package, required beside the module it observes.
reasons.P2-02 packages/kernel/trust-kernel/src/i: HOT ZONE: must[1] required real key material in `signatureRoots`, which is minted in the kernel entry point. This epic changed construction there — an Ed25519 keypair per kernel in a module-private WeakMap — under the P2-02 acceptance lock, and the change is recorded in that lock rather than only here.
reasons.P2-03 packages/core/session/src/index.ts: HOT ZONE: the session log is where a manifest becomes durable, and must[1] requires the manifest appended BEFORE policy. The epic contributes an event type through the documented map rather than changing the log itself.
reasons.P4-06 packages/collaboration/intake-dedu: Created by this epic under ruling §12.5 B: the single (id, epoch) rule both consumers now import, replacing two implementations (BLOCKED-136). The plan predates the finding.
The new package barrel, forced by the repository convention that every packages/*/* directory carries an index.ts entry (B4(f) scaffold).
reasons.P4-06 packages/collaboration/mailbox/src: P5-11 OWNS THIS FILE. Changed here so its second copy of the dedup rule becomes an import of the shared one; the mailbox keeps its own address check and its exported names, and P5-11's four live frozen cases pass unchanged in the same observation (BLOCKED-059 precedent).
reasons.P4-06 packages/run/message-bus/src/bus-s: The durable store must[0] names: one BEGIN IMMEDIATE over the domain event, its outbox rows and the inbox claim. Created by this epic after the clause was reworded (C13) to exclude the KV seam.
reasons.P4-06 packages/run/message-bus/src/dispa: The dispatch loop that turns outbox rows into delivery attempts, which is the at-least-once half of the clause.
reasons.P4-06 packages/run/message-bus/src/mailb: must[2]'s production call site: a real mailbox arrival decided against the durable consumed set. It lives in this package rather than in dsh-mailbox because the store is orchestration-runtime and the mailbox is a capability definition (ruling §12.5 B).
reasons.P4-07 packages/core/agent/src/index.ts: HOT ZONE: the agent entry point re-exports the lifecycle transition the clause fences. The epic adds the fenced variant beside the existing export; the unfenced one is still published and is P4-07's standing open finding.
reasons.P4-08 packages/workflow/workflow-journal: The observer that turns journal records into an observable stream, which the U stage's clause is about.
The recorder that writes journal entries. The registry named the journal package without naming where a record is produced.
reasons.P4-09 packages/workflow/workflow-registr: Nesting-depth decisions, which is the subject of the U-stage clause.
The registry store the P-stage clause persists through.
reasons.P5-10 packages/subagent/subagent/src/con: Convergence decisions for a delegated run, created by this epic as the C-stage contract module.
The router that applies those decisions, created by this epic as the Provider half.
The types both halves share; separated because src/types.ts contains only types by repository rule.
reasons.P5-10 packages/subagent/subagent/src/ind: The package barrel, which must re-export the control surface for any consumer to reach it.
reasons.P6-01 packages/context/memory-context/sr: The context contributor whose recall query the clause constrains.
reasons.P6-02 packages/memory/memory/src/index.t: The memory service the clause is about; the registry declared the package and not its entry point.
reasons.P6-07 packages/session-query/session-que: The corpus assembly the search clause queries over.
The query and result types the corpus and its callers share.
reasons.P6-07 packages/session/session-lifecycle: The lifecycle store the P-stage clause persists through.
reasons.P8-01 scripts/gen-control-protocol-schem: The generator for the control-protocol schema the frozen case compares against. A generated artifact cannot be frozen without naming its generator.
